rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to retain early compounds while eluting strongly retained ones. The retention window and weakest resolutions will guide gradient trimming and subsequent slope and temperature tests.
Lengthen the gradient to test whether the sole underresolved pair responds to reduced slope. The current last peak at 8.30 minutes leaves room to improve separation without incurring a time penalty.

The weak pair improved with a shallower gradient; narrowing the solvent window should move its resolution toward 1.5. Raising the starting organic fraction modestly should offset the longer retention from the reduced slope, keeping the last peak near or below 10 minutes.

Narrow the gradient window one more step to bring the remaining weak pair above R = 1.5. The higher starting organic fraction should largely offset the shallower slope’s effect on the last peak, while the early pairs have ample resolution margin.
Injection 4 already achieved the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Increase temperature by 5 C to seek a shorter fully resolved run while testing the critical pair’s temperature sensitivity.

Return to the temperature that achieved maximum CRF and raise the starting organic fraction to shorten retention. The slightly shallower gradient should help preserve critical-pair resolution, while the early peaks have separation margin.

Test whether higher temperature moves the critical compounds past their apparent convergence and restores separation in a shorter run. This also checks for new limiting pairs, with injection 4 retained as the maximum-score benchmark.

Test the intermediate temperature to balance the two temperature-sensitive separations: the original critical pair has reopened at 60 C, but another pair has converged. At 55 C, both may clear R = 1.5 while retaining the shorter elution time.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness to lift the R = 1.41 pair above baseline resolution, while checking that the neighboring R = 1.74 pair remains resolved. The 8.54-minute last peak leaves ample room for a modest retention increase without a time penalty.

Injection 9 achieves maximum CRF; now test a broader, steeper gradient to shorten the run. Lowering the starting organic fraction may preserve the temperature-sensitive middle-pair separation while also improving early retention.
Shorten the gradient by two minutes to seek a faster method with the same maximum CRF. This isolates the slope response of the two closest pairs, currently at R = 1.77 and 1.57.

Reduce the endpoint to recover the slope-sensitive pair’s resolution while retaining the shorter gradient duration. This slope lies between injections 10 and 11, making full resolution plausible with a last peak earlier than injection 10.

Use a slightly steeper slope than injection 12 to shorten elution while targeting R ≥ 1.5 for both limiting pairs. The endpoint remains above the estimated organic fraction at the last peak, so all compounds should still elute within the gradient.

Test a substantially faster high-temperature gradient on the opposite side of the middle-pair selectivity crossover. The steeper slope may separate the pair that nearly coeluted in injection 7 after reversing its order; injection 13 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test a steeper gradient to further separate the pair that reopened in injection 14, while lowering the starting organic fraction to retain and spread the early-to-middle peaks. This explores a faster separation regime; injection 13 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity using the original scouting gradient, since the fastest high-temperature trials introduced multiple weak pairs. Cooling may separate the central cluster differently and reveal another route to full resolution within 10 minutes.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction improves the reversed middle-pair separation seen in injection 14 while shortening retention further. Early-pair resolution is the main risk, so this run will establish whether that faster solvent window is viable.

Return to the fully resolved regime of injection 9 and slightly reduce the slope to seek more resolution margin at the maximum CRF. The last peak is projected to remain below 10 minutes, while the two limiting pairs should be near R = 1.7.

Test whether lowering the starting organic fraction permits a steeper gradient while preserving the middle-pair separation that limited injection 11. This could shorten the fastest fully resolved run, though the other close pair must also remain above R = 1.5.

Explore whether a steeper gradient at 50 C shifts the original critical pair past coelution while avoiding the new overlap seen at 60 C. Injection 19 already secures maximum CRF; this trial targets a substantially shorter fully resolved method.

Shorten injection 19’s gradient by two minutes to test the faster boundary of its fully resolved regime. This isolates slope effects at the most promising temperature and starting composition, with particular attention to the two close middle pairs.

Preserve injection 19’s successful slope while ending the gradient earlier, just above the estimated last-peak elution composition. This should retain maximum CRF and the 7.60-minute last peak with a shorter programmed gradient.

Keep the successful gradient slope through the closely spaced peaks, then test a lower-organic hold for the well-separated final compound. This may preserve maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient and lower solvent strength, provided the last peak remains within 10 minutes.

Test intermediate low-temperature selectivity between the 30 C run with several overlaps and the 40 C run with just one weak pair. This unexplored temperature may balance the central separations while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes; maximum CRF is already secured.

Preserve injection 12’s fully resolved slope while trimming the gradient endpoint to just above the last peak’s estimated elution composition. This should retain CRF 1.000 and approximately 8.00-minute final elution, with slightly more resolution margin than the fastest demonstrated method.
